title: Today on X
windowLabel: 7:00 a.m. Wednesday, Nov. 18 to 7:01 a.m. Thursday, Nov. 19, B.C. time
method: Built from the News & Events brief's X summary, then each post was re-read on X this morning to confirm the wording and counts. Counts may have changed since. The brief covered 1,862 timeline posts from 219 accounts (replies excluded). Elliotte Friedman's post came from a separate public search, since we don't follow him.
trendsNote: X’s worldwide list often reflects the most active regions at this hour, which is why it may look different from the Canada and U.S. lists.

themes.title: Trump, Putin and Xi: the first three-way meeting
themes.summary: @WhiteHouse posted video of Trump meeting Putin in China ("We've known each other for a long time"), and @bennyjohnson posted Trump's full remarks from what he called the "historic first Trilateral meeting." The meeting happened: the BBC and AP report the three leaders talked at a villa in Shenzhen on the sidelines of APEC and issued a joint declaration saying nuclear war "cannot be won and must never be fought." The declaration does not mention Ukraine or Iran.
themes.whyItMatters: It was the biggest diplomatic story of the day on the feed, and it is today's lead.

flags.label: Confirmed
flags.note: Reported by the BBC and AP; the White House published the declaration.

source.title: White House: U.S.-Russia-China heads of state declaration toward peace

related.title: Trump, Xi and Putin hold first three-way meeting, pledge nuclear-risk talks

themes.title: Musk on Russia, Ukraine and Starlink at DealBook
themes.summary: @bennyjohnson posted clips of Elon Musk at the New York Times DealBook Summit, quoting him saying "Russia is the aggressor" but that the U.S. "staged a coup" in Ukraine in 2014, and that Zelenskyy "is not always truthful." Musk did say these things, according to The Verge and Ukrainska Pravda, which report he argued Starlink should not be used for offensive drone strikes.
themes.whyItMatters: The quotes are real; the claims inside them are Musk's opinions.

flags.label: Confirmed
flags.note: Musk made the remarks, per The Verge.

source.title: The Verge: Musk on Ukraine, Starlink and Starshield at DealBook

flags.label: Disputed
flags.note: The "coup" claim and the charge that Zelenskyy is lying are Musk's assertions, not established facts.

themes.title: Bartow, Fla., council meeting erupts over a Muslim invocation
themes.summary: @libsoftiktok posted that residents in Bartow, Fla., "COUNTERED" an imam's opening prayer by reciting the Lord's Prayer. That happened, but the post leaves out how it ended: WFLA reports police removed people who wouldn't stop, with no arrests, and the imam finished about 10 minutes later. The city says its invocation is open to all faiths.
themes.whyItMatters: A Florida story where the full account matters.

flags.label: Partly true
flags.note: The disruption happened; the post omits that the imam finished the prayer.

source.title: WFLA: Imam's invocation at Bartow city meeting disrupted

themes.title: Former Erie Democratic chair, never a U.S. citizen, leaves for Nova Scotia
themes.summary: @libsoftiktok posted that Ian Murray, a former Erie County Democratic chairman and DNC member, was "forced to LEAVE" the U.S. The Erie Times-News reports he was never a U.S. citizen — federal authorities ruled his Canadian-born mother didn't meet a residency rule in the 1940 Nationality Act — and that he left for Nova Scotia on Nov. 12. The newspaper says he learned of the ruling when he applied for a passport. As a non-citizen who had been living and working in the United States, he was there without legal status, and he has now left.
themes.whyItMatters: A Canadian angle: he has moved to Nova Scotia.

flags.label: Confirmed
flags.note: Reported by the Erie Times-News and The Center Square.

themes.title: Florida license examiner faces 360 felony counts
themes.summary: @catturd2 quoted a report on the arrest of a Florida driver-license employee, and @libsoftiktok posted that the state's CFO confirmed the licenses involved were revoked. Florida Highway Patrol says the Pembroke Pines examiner was arrested Nov. 16 and faces 360 felony counts over 60 licenses allegedly issued to unqualified applicants through a driving school. Bond was set at $15,000.
themes.whyItMatters: A Florida licensing case that could affect other licences issued through the same school.

flags.label: Confirmed
flags.note: Reported by CBS Miami and NBC 6; ClickOrlando reports the CFO said the licenses were revoked.

source.title: CBS Miami: Broward DMV worker faces 360 charges

themes.title: New Jersey non-citizen voter registrations: true, but from July
themes.summary: @ScottPresler posted that Gov. Mikie Sherrill revealed New Jersey registered 6,600 non-citizens to vote and 400 voted. The AP reported this in July: a motor-vehicle software error between June 2023 and June 2024 registered about 6,600 people who said they weren't citizens, and fewer than 400 of them voted.
themes.whyItMatters: Accurate numbers, but old news presented as new.

source.title: AP: Noncitizen voter registration in New Jersey

themes.title: El Salvador strikes Haitian gang leader's home
themes.summary: @DailyLoud posted that Salvadoran troops destroyed the "$9.3 MILLION mansion" of Haitian gang leader Jeff Larose. The AP reports President Bukele announced the strike and said Salvadoran helicopters fired on the home in Canaan, north of Port-au-Prince. It is unclear whether Larose was inside.

themes.title: DOJ probe in Alaska Senate race
themes.summary: @bennyjohnson posted that the DOJ issued "over 200 subpoenas" in an Alaska Senate election investigation. A Justice Department spokesperson told the Anchorage Daily News a federal probe "remains underway"; it centres on Republican claims that Mary Peltola's side recruited the namesake candidate "Decoy Dan" J. Sullivan, which her campaign denies. Dan J. Sullivan got 1.7% of first-choice votes, far less than Peltola's margin.
themes.whyItMatters: The investigation is real; the subpoena count comes from unnamed sources.

flags.label: Confirmed
flags.note: A federal probe exists, per the Anchorage Daily News.

source.title: Anchorage Daily News: GOP-led investigations still underway

flags.note: The "over 200 subpoenas" figure comes from Fox News' unnamed sources.

themes.summary: @libsoftiktok posted that Albemarle County Public Schools are closed until after Thanksgiving. The district confirms schools are closed to students from Thursday, Nov. 19, through the break; VPM reports more than 500 hires had never been checked against Virginia's child-abuse registry.

themes.title: UK asks Google to remove Russell Brand prison message
themes.summary: @TRobinsonNewEra posted that the UK government asked Google to take down Russell Brand's YouTube account. The BBC reports the government did ask Google to remove his prison message, but Google declined, saying its rules weren't broken. Reports differ on whether the request covered the whole account or just the video.

flags.label: Partly true
flags.note: The request was made; nothing was removed, and its scope is unclear.

themes.title: NHL trade watch: quiet day
themes.summary: No trades were completed in the past 24 hours. @FriedgeHNIC (Elliotte Friedman) posted that Anaheim put Travis Mitchell on waivers. On Oilers Now, Friedman said the Oilers aren't interested in Blues goalie Jordan Binnington and that Edmonton's needs are a top-four defenceman and fourth-line depth, the Edmonton Journal reports. Friedman's account is not one we follow; we checked it separately.
themes.whyItMatters: Insider commentary, not reported trade talks.

flags.label: Unverified
flags.note: Friedman's Oilers comments are insider commentary; nobody has reported active Oilers trade talks.
